utterances.text: Did you use those reports to write this article P699?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Some of them I will have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when they told you about this opposition and fighting, you accepted it as true, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I accepted it as the opinions of those who filed their information. Whether it is true or not is not for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move on. If I might have one moment, Your Honour. Let me cover a few things that were covered on direct examination dealing with your reports, and in paragraph 33 Mr. Russo -- and the report that I'm talking about is 695. I apologise, sir. That's your report of 12/12/95, and I believe you were quoted that the 7th -- the middle of paragraph 33 -- are you with me, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I am indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And again if I get ahead, just please stop me. "7th Puma Brigade was the first to enter the town. All the HV military vehicles had stickers on denoting this. The first vehicles in were the tanks and the APCs. They arrived in a convoy and were not moving tactically because of this. I don't think they were expecting much resistance. At about 1300, trucks and jeeps arrived." Now, sir, what time -- I'm sorry. What time did the 7th Puma Brigade arrive in Knin that you observed and what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I don't know. It would be sometime on the date that I put in here, so sometime on the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well you note here that the jeeps came at 1300?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Trucks and jeeps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that about the time the Puma Brigade came?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Reading that text, I suspect it was prior to that but not by much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately when?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I don't know. Sometime in the previous couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So sometime between 11.00 and 1.00?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I'm happy to accept that approximation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you wrote this --

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I don't know when I wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm just waiting for the --

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry. When you wrote this, sir --

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- did you know that the HV was already at the hospital and inside by 11.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if they were in radio communication and if they were in the hospital, it would be reasonable for the HV, as they were driving through, to conclude that they weren't going to face any resistance; right?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: No, because I believe the hospital is some way out from the centre of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How far?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I'd have to look at the map to be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were they carrying radios?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The HV have radios?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: The ones at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The ones that you saw.

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Okay. The ones that I saw on the tanks or the trucks, and the jeeps?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Anywhere.

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let's talk for a minute about the shelling of Knin. You noted in your statement, if I may, that when the shelling started, and I'm referring you to -- you to 699. That isn't your statement. It's the article. I apologise. And in the last paragraph it says, "When it came it was a shock and truly terrifying." In the last sentence: "And within seconds my actions were those of someone who was terrified and in a state of panic." I think you told us this morning that you went down for the first hour and a half or so and you were in bunker; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I went down there from about 5.00 till 6.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last paragraph of what, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Last paragraph of the -- the article of -- I apologise, Judge. This is the 699, The Fall of the Republic of the Serb Krajina. It's on the second page of this article, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So for the first hour and a half you have no knowledge exactly what was being targeted HV fire, do you?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, Knin in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: No, but it sounded like it. It was rockets and shells of considerable proportion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know what was in fact hit at 5.00 in the morning or between 5.00 and 6.30?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I could not identify anything specifically as I was in the bunker.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you came out of the bunker you noted that there was a tremendous amount of smoke. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dangerfield, Mr. Kehoe asked you whether that's right. Of course he quotes you because you've said that. He's seeking confirmation that what you said is what you meant to say, and then the answer, "I did say that," does not give the information Mr. Kehoe is seeking. At the same time, Mr. Kehoe, the witness has, of course, already testified as to the accuracy and -- so therefore you often start asking whether something is right when you could move on more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of -- P695, your 1990 -- I apologise, 1995 statement. This is on page 7 of P695, in the centre of the page. You -- if I may, we're just going to bring this up on the screen. Can we go to the next page on that, please. I think there's a B/C/S -- that's the page. If we just go to the middle of the page, there, the top -- excuse me. Just down a little bit. Okay. Let me see. That's good. About midway down of that paragraph of paragraph 30. It notes: "The town of Knin." Do you see that, sir? "The town of Knin was also covered by so much dust?"

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "The town of Knin was covered with so much dust and smoke from the shelling that no one would have been able to see where the rounds were landing unless they were standing in the immediate vicinity of the impacts." Now, where do you say in this statement that the smoke cleared and that you were able to see the point of impacts? Please look through this, or if you know off the top of your head I'd invite you to tell us where that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but if counsel knows it's not in there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's not in there. If you stipulate to that we'll move on. It's not in there, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'll stipulate to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a photograph that's in evidence, and it is -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just explain this, Judge. It's actually D569, but if, Madam Usher, you could bring it up as 1D380203. This is one of those photographs, Judge, that we had put in through Sanction, and I don't think it was uploaded between the time we used it and the time of ... If we could blow that up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, that is photograph that was on the left-hand side OTP taken of -- in late November -- or November of last year. I'm not certain of the exact date, counsel. And then the last one is one taken at the same time both from the balcony area of the headquarters for UN Sector South. Now, just looking at the first one on the right-hand side with the smoke in the distance, that was essentially the viewpoint that you had when you were looking into downtown Knin, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I don't recognise this photo, and I don't recognise what time of the day it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you talked to us -- I can offer to you that this was taken into the early morning hours during the attack. It was presented in a video coming from the OTP. But your viewpoint going into Knin was -- looking at the photograph on the left, that would be a viewpoint going into downtown Knin. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I don't remember the viewpoint from the balcony looking into Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: And I don't recognise that photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, when you were offering testimony this morning about the areas of impact in Knin, you have no idea of what was actually impacted, do you?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I do, because when I stood on the balcony and viewed it I was using binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Binoculars. You didn't say that this morning, did you? So you were with binoculars and the smoke cleared; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I think -- I think you said, sir, that the -- this photo, you know, is an early morning shot. I certainly recall being able to stand wherever I did on that headquarters. The smoke had lifted, and when I was viewing through my binoculars, when I could and when the time allowed, I could see the areas, not the precise impact point, but the areas as I circled on the map where the rounds were falling. So, yes, I can say that the rounds were falling into those residential areas categorically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Categorically. Let's pull up P62. Now, sir, in your statement of -- before we go to this, of 695, you offered us, one, two, three, four, five -- six various targets, and I'm talking about paragraph 26 of your statement, and you left out or you didn't designate the headquarters of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina. Where is it?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: There's something wrong with this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it's the photo you used to circle this -- it's the same photo you used to circle under P697 this morning. The same one.

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: It just doesn't look similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well let's go back to 697, P697. We'll use that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Usher. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you recognise that one, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: It may be similar. I'm prepared to say that I believe it's a different resolution, and so it may -- it certainly appears different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What appears different?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: The two pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not photoed well on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the witness may have problems zooming in and zooming out, and what you see on the screen is not what you see if you're marking something on a desk or a table, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where is the headquarters of the army of Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: I can't comment on that. All I can comment on are the various locations that are printed on the map, on the map that I have signed and the residential areas that I have located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dangerfield, a question is put to you, and I'd -- if you say, "I can't comment on that," the issue is not whether you feel that you can comment on it but whether you know the answer to the question. The question was: Where is the headquarters of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina? Do you know or do you not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the actual targets that you gave us, and in paragraph 26. Could you go to paragraph 26? You gave us a series of items with a six-digit grid, and that's -- we know from other witnesses that the six-digit grids is a hundred metres by a hundred metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROLAND DANGERFIELD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's look at the grid reference that you -- if we could put 1D420001 on the screen. If we can spin that, please. The other way. Sorry. Now, this is a grid reference you gave us in C for the general supply, and the grid reference you gave us within a hundred metres is 363775.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The -- looking at this series of pictures in this exhibit, it appears that, and correct me if I'm wrong, Counsel, that they're going to put to the witness that the areas that he's identified, the grid square references that he's identified, are different from the areas where he identifies that they are using this Google image map. I'm not aware of, and certainly we'd like to know what the foundation for the fact that the grid square reference can be placed on using Google Earth; specifically, that the grid square reference that he used when he picked the map can be superimposed on an image from which we don't know the elevation and we don't the other factors. In other words, they're going to put to him that this is correct and what you said was incorrect. I'd like some foundation laid for the fact that this is correct, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Grid references are grid references no matter where you go and what you do, and the grid references are within -- the six-digit grid references put in by the witness are within a hundred metres of one another. All one need do is go out and look at the grid references given by the witness and compare it to the grid references on the map, and I will tell you categorically that on the five grid reference that he put down he's 0 for 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would agree that grid square references are uniform; however, they're uniform to uniform maps. This is not a map, this is a satellite image for which we don't know the elevation at which it's taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now I have to shed my own light and please correct me when I'm wrong. Grid references refer to a division in squares of the earth surface. Now, if you have a larger map, the -- that means a scale with a lower number, 1:5.000, 1:10.000, then the grid references, the grid rectangulars appear larger on the map as everything appears larger on that map. So to that extent when you have a larger map the grid references will enlarge with it, and if you take a map with more precision, a scale lower than the previous one, then it will adapt. So therefore, it does not depend on the maps. The grid reference will always appear on the same location on the map. Otherwise, you might have a problem, because if you manipulate the maps seriously enough then Rome suddenly would be New York. Let's proceed. Mr. Russo, if there's any reason to correct my understanding of this, please do so, but I'm usually rather hesitant to give my own views on matters. But if you agree then please feel free, or think it over perhaps during the night, because it's 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will continue with grid references tomorrow morning. But, Mr. Dangerfield, first I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony, whether that's the testimony you gave today or whether that's the testimony still to be given tomorrow. We -- we'd like to see you back, and we will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00 in this same courtroom.
